npm.integrity_format: sha512-<base64> (npm registry `integrity` field value; sha1-<base64> accepted for legacy rows)
npm.allowlist_semantics: allowlist=true = pinned and trusted (change requires human review); allowlist=false = known-untrusted, finding always; absent = unpinned, finding (severity medium)
npm.changes: any add, remove, or version/integrity bump requires a human-reviewed diff; automated update (e.g. `npm audit fix --force`, `npm update`) is forbidden unless the resulting diff passes human review

github_refs.commit_sha_format: full 40-hex (SHA-1) or 64-hex (SHA-256) commit SHA; short SHAs are invalid (moved-tag/malleable-ref defense)
github_refs.allowlist_semantics: allowlist=true = pinned and trusted (change requires human review); allowlist=false = known-untrusted, finding always; absent = unpinned or floating ref (branch/range), finding (severity high)
github_refs.changes: any add, remove, or commit_sha change requires a human-reviewed diff; `git verify-tag` is not a substitute for SHA pinning (moved tags), it is a supplement

policy.rebaseline: requires a human-reviewed diff; never auto-accepted; every re-baseline is recorded with owner, rationale, and date
human_review_covers: version intent: exact-semver pin vs floating range
integrity/provenance: registry integrity field, npm provenance (Sigstore), signed tags
install scripts: presence of postinstall/preinstall/install in the pinned version's manifest
publisher identity: npm maintainer / GitHub owner verified, not typosquat
license and declared dependencies of the pinned artifact
lockfile diff accompanying the pin change

rules.label: INJ-OBFUSC
rules.known_fp_note: npm integrity fields (sha512-...) and lockfile hashes are legitimate base64 blobs; excluded as documented known-FP class (02f §10, Nina FP budget)
known_fp_classes: camelCase-acronym word runs joined by single / (e.g. Substitute/Combine/Adapt)
URL fragments with repeated slashes or dots (file://, raw.githubusercontent.com)
rules.note: F-3 (Victor): looksLikeBase64 guard (digit-or-symbol + mixed case + no // and no .) reduced repo-wide FPs 87 -> 3 on .agents. Remaining 3 = documented FP classes above; not suppressed further to avoid masking real blobs.

rules.label: INJ-ROLE
rules.pattern: you are now (the )?(system|root|superuser)|act as (the )?system\b|new system prompt:

rules.label: INJ-PATH
rules.note: applied to filenames + interpolated identifiers only, never full prose (supply-chain-audit-spec.md line 183; QA F-1)

entropy.note: threshold 2.6 (max achievable for 8 distinct chars is 3.0; 3.5 was unreachable — rule could never fire). Regex match with entropy < threshold is NOT a finding (negative fixture: AKIA + repeated chars -> ~0.0).

rules.label: S16-BEACON
rules.note: F-4 (Victor): extended to pwsh/iex/cmd + sudo; iex is canonical PowerShell download-exec

fault_contract.note: Exit 2 (fail-closed) is triggered by tool/environment failure, NOT by harness-shaped content. Negative fixtures (harness-shaped unknown dirs) must exit 0.

fault_inputs.trigger: npm audit/OSV/socket.dev subprocess killed or non-zero

fp_metric.numerator: informational findings := rule hits labeled severity low OR known-FP-class (documented per-rule known-FP notes)
fp_metric.denominator: corpus files × harness shapes per run (baseline-corpus executions)
fp_metric.formula: FP rate = numerator ÷ denominator, frozen corpus only, per harness shape
fp_metric.gate: NEW-FINDINGS-ONLY vs frozen baseline; new findings labeled, never auto-baselined

known_fp_excludes.note: Path globs whose matches are documented-FP-prone; scanner must not report these paths for the listed rules (02f §10, QA F-9).
